parts.note_add: On 1982 power-window cars each door has its own 4-pin switch (I-06 LH: RL, B, GL, BL; I-07 RH: R, B, G, BL) on a 30 A IG fuse (S-001 p28); FA03-66-350A is one switch that serves either side, still sold new (Atkins, 2026).

Single-wire horn: GY from the horn relay F-16, grounded through its bracket; shares the 15 A fuse with the stop lights (S-001 p22). The 1980 manual sets each horn to 3.0 +/- 0.5 A at 12 V with its adjusting screw.

Single-wire horn: GY from the horn relay F-16, grounded through its bracket; shares the 15 A fuse with the stop lights (S-001 p22). Which of F-09/F-10 is the low tone is not shown in S-001; confirm on the car.

The 1982 system (S-001 p14, section B): main switch B-31 on a 10 A IG fuse (Br) feeds BrB to the unit B-25 and the actuator B-28; stop B-26 and clutch B-27 switches (Br/RY) cancel; set/coast/resume on the combination switch B-30; vehicle speed switch B-29 (BR).
A vacuum servo with three solenoid coils (VAC, VENT 1, VENT 2) on a common BrB feed (S-001 p14; coil names from the 1985 manual).
The actuator inner cable pulls the carburettor throttle lever; free play is set at an adjusting nut (1985 manual 15-51).
13-cavity connector B-25 (12 wires, one cavity unused) (S-001 p14); the 1985 manual tests it through its 13-pin plug with the ACC checker 49 9200 010.
Three momentary contacts SET (BY), COAST (RW) and RESUME (BrW), each to a common B ground, at connector B-30 (S-001 p14).
The main switch it caps carries a 3.4 W indicator lamp (S-001 p14).
